name: Morva Matcha-Coconut Chew Bars
description: Chewy synth-nougat bars with a matcha-infused base and shredded coconut analog layered through the center. Dense, filling, and positioned as a between-meal snack rather than a pure confection.
flavor_profile: Grassy, slightly bitter matcha throughout; sweet coconut cream in the chewy center layer; the nougat is dense and slightly sticky; mild vanilla-adjacent finish
cultural_context: Popular with workers who can't take proper meal breaks. The matcha bitterness makes it feel slightly virtuous, which is part of its appeal — it's candy that doesn't fully feel like candy. Nutrition data on the wrapper is technically accurate but formatted to obscure the synth-protein filler content.
story_hooks: Morva has been quietly reducing bar size by 4% every six months for three years — a consumer advocate just published the measurements
The coconut analog compound in current production runs is sourced from a supplier under investigation for labor violations in their synthesis facilities
A Morva bar is the last thing a missing Shelf worker was seen buying on transit kiosk footage — the bar itself may hold trace evidence
